html:
Domingo Faustino Sarmiento was an Argentine writer, educator and president of Argentina from 1868 to 1874. He believed that schools would turn the country into a modern nation.

Born in San Juan, he fought against Rosas and went into exile in Chile. There in 1845 he wrote Facundo, a portrait of a provincial warlord, which set civilisation, the cities and Europe, against barbarism, the plains, the gauchos and the caudillos. It became a classic of Latin American writing.

As president he founded hundreds of schools, brought American women teachers to train Argentine ones, and ran the first national census. He encouraged European immigration and railways. His contempt for gauchos and Indigenous people is criticised today. Teachers' Day in Argentina is held on the day of his death, and José Hernández answered his view of the gaucho in Martín Fierro.
